observability._note: Decidesk adopts the OpenRegister AppHost observability engine (ADR-040 / ADR-006). The /api/health route is served by a thin GenericHealthController subclass (HealthController) that reshapes the engine result into the published REQ-API-004 body {status, baseUrl, version, openregister}; /api/metrics is aliased straight to GenericMetricsController. statusCodePolicy=always200 + cors=true reproduce the REQ-API-004 reverse-proxy probe contract (probes succeed even when degraded; CORS + OPTIONS preflight). The orAvailable check subsumes the former hand-rolled DI-container ObjectService lookup. No metrics[] descriptors: decidesk gains the implicit decidesk_info / decidesk_up gauges, a pure compliance upgrade over the no-metrics-endpoint baseline.

config._note: Governance body (council, committee, board) — the standing organiser that owns meetings, members and a process template. Bespoke layout: body details lead (mandate, quorum rule, voting default, term dates, hourly rate) 8-wide with the Members roster surfaced right (member management is the daily task on a body), then the body's meetings as a full-width object-list so a clerk sees the meeting cadence at a glance, and a Documents leaf for charters/standing orders. Process template, efficiency analytics, recording retention and audit trail are specialist/rare surfaces kept in sidebar tabs.

Meeting — the operational hub of the app: the event that runs an agenda, gathers participants, produces minutes and decisions. Bespoke meeting-workspace layout: meeting details (type, mode, schedule, location, chair, quorum, cost) lead 8-wide with the live Participants roster right (who is expected/attending is the first thing a clerk checks); the ordered Agenda (agenda-item children keyed on `meeting`) sits full-width as the working document; Decisions taken and Minutes drafted render below as the meeting's outputs; a Documents leaf holds packets/attachments. No comms leaf on the body (the meeting schema declares no email/calendar/talk linkedType; calendar/Talk stay in the Integrations surface). Recurring Series, Transcription, Votes aggregate, Publication and audit trail are specialist tabs.

pages.title: Meeting integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this meeting — the Action items board (Deck), Discussion (Talk), files and notes surface on the body; linked articles, tags and the audit trail remain in the sidebar.

pages._note: Comms/collaboration workspace for a meeting — the ADR-019 integration surface, deliberately distinct from the MeetingDetail record page. The leaves promoted onto the body are exactly the providers bound to the meeting object through the registry: the Deck action-items board (migrate-action-items-to-deck-leaf), projecting the CalDAV VTODO ActionItems (ADR-002 source of truth) as cards and replacing the retired in-app TaskService/DelegationService board; Discussion (Talk); meeting Files and Notes. Comms leaves are legitimate here because these are the meeting's registry-bound integration providers. The useRegistry sidebar still lists every provider and hides each gracefully when its backing app is absent — action items then remain reachable via the Nextcloud Tasks app over the same VTODOs.

pages.title: Decision integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this decision dossier — linked Emails, the Action items board (Deck) and files surface on the body; notes, tags and the audit trail remain in the sidebar.

pages._note: Email linking is consumed from the ADR-019 Email integration leaf bound to the decision object (migrate-email-links-to-email-leaf), replacing the retired in-app EmailLink store. The Action items board is consumed from the ADR-019 Deck integration leaf bound to the decision object (migrate-action-items-to-deck-leaf), projecting CalDAV VTODO ActionItems (ADR-002) as cards and replacing the retired in-app TaskService/DelegationService board. The registry hides each tab gracefully when its backing app is absent — action items then remain reachable via the Nextcloud Tasks app over the same VTODOs.

pages.title: Agenda item integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this agenda item — linked Emails, files and tasks surface on the body; notes, tags and the audit trail remain in the sidebar.

pages._note: Email linking is consumed from the ADR-019 Email integration leaf bound to the agenda-item object (migrate-email-links-to-email-leaf), replacing the retired in-app EmailLink store. Registry hides the Email tab gracefully when Mail is absent.

pages.title: Live meeting
pages._note: Realtime meeting shell — WebSocket subscriptions, frame-by-frame UI, per-vote-card animations. No typed primitive analogue; documented as the canonical example for a future type:realtime lib extension. See src/views/LiveMeeting.vue.

config._note: Participant — a person archetype (name, role, party, email, voting weight, attendance, linked Nextcloud user, join/leave dates). Bespoke person layout: contact/role details lead 8-wide with Related right (the meetings, votes and decisions this person is linked to across the register); a Documents leaf holds credentials/mandate letters. Deliberately NO Email or Calendar body leaf: the participant schema declares no email/calendar linkedType (the email address is a plain data field, and correspondence lives on the meeting/decision integration surfaces, not per-participant), so per the comms-leaf hard rule they are omitted. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab.

Agenda item — one ordered line of a meeting's agenda (type, order number, estimated/actual duration, description, recurrence, parent item). Bespoke layout: item details lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for the supporting stukken (memo, annex) that back the item; the Motions tabled under this item (AgendaMotionsTab — decisions of decisionType=motion keyed on `agendaItem`) render full-width below because debating/voting motions is the whole point of an agenda item. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab; email/files linking lives on the dedicated AgendaItemIntegrations surface.

Motion — a deliberative proposal (a Decision of decisionType=motion): proposer, motion type, proposed text, lifecycle, co-signers, submission date. Bespoke deliberation layout: motion details/text lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for the tabled text and annexes; the Amendments proposed against it (MotionAmendmentsTab — decisions keyed on `parentMotion`) render full-width because processing amendments is the core motion workflow; the Votes result (MotionVotesTab, read-only post-ballot aggregate) sits below. The chair's amendment Voting order and the Voting round mechanics are procedural/rare and stay sidebar tabs, as does the audit trail. Discussion/Talk lives on the dedicated MotionIntegrations surface.

pages.title: Motion integrations

config.description: External integrations linked to this motion — open the sidebar for Discussion (Talk), files, notes, tags, tasks and the audit trail.

pages._note: Discussion is consumed from the ADR-019 Talk integration leaf bound to the motion object (migrate-comments-to-talk-leaf), replacing the retired in-app CommentService. Registry hides the Talk tab gracefully when Talk is absent.

config._note: Amendment — a proposed text change to a parent motion (a Decision of decisionType=amendment): proposed text, proposer, parent motion reference, voting order. Bespoke amendment layout: the visual Text-changes diff against the parent motion (AmendmentDiffTab) is the reason this record exists, so it leads full-width; the amendment's own metadata (proposer, lifecycle, order) sits 8-wide below with the Parent motion link (AmendmentParentMotionTab) right so a clerk can jump back to the motion being amended. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab. No comms leaf — the amendment schema declares none; discussion happens on the parent motion.

Minutes — the formal document record of a meeting (title, lifecycle, content, version, signers, approval date, generated documents). Bespoke document archetype: minutes metadata leads 8-wide with the Approval workflow (MinutesApprovalTab — lifecycle timeline with guarded submit/approve/reject and correction suggestions) right, because getting minutes approved is the primary task on this record; the generated Documents (MinutesDocumentTab — PDF/notarial packages written into the meeting Files folder) render full-width below as the tangible output. Signers roster, Publication and audit trail are lower-frequency and stay sidebar tabs. No comms leaf — the minutes schema declares none.

config._motionsFilterNote: REQ-RMN-003 — Motions is one decisionType of the unified Decision supertype (ADR-005), not a sibling concept. This quick-filter surfaces Motions AS a filtered view of Decisions (decisionType=motion, a STORED/queryable field merged server-side into the OpenRegister fetch — no client-side derivation, unlike effectiveStatus per the _inForceFilterNote). The retained Motions index page (pages[] id `Motions`, route /motions) carries the same filter plus motion-specific columns/tabs; the `page`/`route` hints let the strip deep-link there. The standalone top-level Motions menu leaf was retired (REQ-RMN-001) so Motions is reachable through its parent Decisions surface rather than as a peer top-level item.
config._inForceFilterNote: DESIGN D3 — the in-force filter operates over the derived effectiveStatus, which (per design D2) is NOT a stored/queryable field: OpenRegister cannot express the inbound supersedes/repeals lookup as a materialised calculation, so effectiveStatus is computed client-side. A static manifest `filter` (the proven Motions decisionType pattern) and `quickFilters` both merge a filter map into the OpenRegister fetch and therefore only work over STORED fields — neither can server-filter on a client-derived value. The in-force / superseded / repealed state is instead surfaced per-decision via the effectiveStatus badge column (computed client-side) plus the banner and incoming-relation groups in RelatedDecisionsTab. A server-side in-force filter becomes available only if/when effectiveStatus is materialised by an OpenRegister inverse-relation calculation operator (D2 follow-up).

config._note: Decision — the core governance dossier (title, text, outcome, decision date, legal basis, lifecycle, publication state, effectiveStatus). Bespoke dossier layout: decision details/text lead 8-wide with the Lifecycle state machine (DecisionLifecycleTab — the guarded transition buttons that advance the decision) right, because moving a decision through its states is the primary action; the Action items it spawns (ActionItemsSurface — the Deck-board projection of children keyed on `decision`, ADR-019/ADR-002) render full-width, then Related decisions (RelatedDecisionsTab — the supersedes/repeals graph driving the computed effectiveStatus banner) and a Documents leaf. Route (approval routing), Voting results, Publication and audit trail are lower-frequency and stay sidebar tabs. Email linking lives on the dedicated DecisionIntegrations surface (schema declares no comms linkedType).

Action item — a task/case archetype spawned by a decision or meeting (title, description, assignee, due date, status, completion). Note the canonical store is a CalDAV VTODO (ADR-002) surfaced through the Deck leaf; this OR-backed detail shows the projected record. Bespoke task layout: task details (status, assignee, due date) lead 8-wide with a Documents leaf right for evidence/deliverables of completion, and Related below linking back to the originating decision/meeting. No comms leaf — the action-item schema declares none; assignment happens via the assignee field. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab.

Collaboration workspace — a bounded faction/committee/task-group space (name, type, access level, created date). Per migrate-workspaces-to-collectives-leaf (ADR-022) the in-app WorkspaceService/CollaborationWorkspace store was retired: the real collaboration surface is a Nextcloud Collective bound through the ADR-019 registry, so the Collectives leaf leads the body (this is the whole point of the workspace) alongside a Files leaf for shared documents, with workspace metadata and Related below. The Collectives leaf is a declared, registry-bound integration for this entity, so it belongs on the body; the registry hides it gracefully when the Collectives app is absent. Audit trail stays a sidebar tab.
